segments.text: In the Encyclopedia of Triangle Centers, the Isogonal Conjugate is the fundamental angular reflection of triangle geometry. Reflecting the three cevians of a point P across the interior angle bisectors A X one, B X one, and C X one yields three new concurrent lines meeting at its isogonal conjugate P star.

segments.text: In homogeneous trilinear coordinates, isogonal conjugation simply takes the reciprocal of each distance: alpha, beta, gamma maps to one over alpha, one over beta, one over gamma. Across Collection One, the Incenter X one is self-isogonal. The Centroid X two and Symmedian Point X six are isogonal conjugates, transforming medians into symmedians. And the Circumcenter X three and Orthocenter X four are isogonal conjugates, reflecting perpendicular bisectors into altitudes.

segments.text: Even the equilateral centers obey isogonal duality: the First and Second Fermat points X thirteen and X fourteen map directly to the First and Second Isodynamic points X fifteen and X sixteen.
